sector_model: exchange and financial technology operator (not a bank): GAAP P/E, EV/revenue, FCF yield, net debt, clearing assets excluded, goodwill share
thesis: Nasdaq, Inc. (Nasdaq: NDAQ) runs exchanges, clearing, listings, index and fintech/regtech software. Q3 2026 total revenues 2,393M (+20.9%), net revenues 1,481M (+12.6%; 9M 4,388M, +13.8%); GAAP operating income 732M (+24.9%), 9M 2,101M vs 1,702M; diluted EPS 0.96 vs 0.73. Segments 9M: Capital Access Platforms +17.3%, Financial Technology +17.2%, Market Services +13.5%. TTM revenue 9,150M, GAAP NI 2,084M, OCF 2,546M, capex 288M, FCF 2,258M, SBC 177M. Debt 8,740M (long-term 8,471M, short-term 269M) vs cash and short-term investments 516M, net debt about 8.2B. At 108.65 (2026-11-12 close; 52-week 76.55-111.45): market cap about 60.3B on 554.96M shares (cover 2026-10-16), EV about 68.5B, 28.9x TTM GAAP earnings, FCF yield 3.7%. Quality recurring business near its 52-week high; not cheap.
counterthesis: At 29x GAAP earnings and a price within 3% of the 52-week high, the market already pays for double-digit net revenue growth. Market Services growth (+26% in Q3) depends on elevated trading volumes and may reverse. Net debt of about 8.2B from the Adenza deal limits flexibility, tax rate rose to 22.9% from 18.9%, 9M includes an 84M divestiture gain, and buybacks accelerated to 1.2B (pace funded partly by commercial paper). TTM revenue combines bases that were restated (9M25 6,138M originally vs 6,175M now). Segment net revenue, ARR, non-GAAP reconciliation, guidance, litigation, Adenza integration and peers (ICE, CME, CBOE, LSEG, TW) unread.
invalidation: Thesis weakens if net revenue growth drops below high single digits when volumes normalize, Financial Technology ARR growth slows, or leverage rises. A valuation case needs a price near a 5% FCF yield or evidence of durable low-teens growth.
